thread:
sam.peopleops: Hey team — quick help needed. Employee had ACL repair on 3/10, went to preferred PT clinic but the claim came back out-of-network. Clinic says it's because their billing TIN/NPI didn't match insurance records. We do have a prior auth: PA-8821 and the clinic submitted it. Claim# 992-PT-551. What do we advise for appealing and getting the clinic to rebill in-network? Also the clinic is asking for a temporary proof-of-coverage letter to start scheduling more sessions this week.

alex.benefits: Ugh. Two threads here — appeal + proof letter. For appeal we usually ask member to confirm dates of service + upload the itemized bill and EOB to the benefits portal. If prior auth exists and matches dates, we escalate to medical review.

lena.peopleops: @alex.benefits can you confirm whether mismatch on TIN/NPI is something we can fix from our side or if clinic needs to resubmit? The member says they signed with the clinic expecting in-network rates.

alex.benefits: Clinic needs to resubmit with corrected billing taxonomy. Insurance looks up provider via NPI/TIN combination at claim time. If provider changed billing entity, claim goes OON. We can email the insurer escalation team pointing at PA-8821 and request reprocessing if clinic resubmits.

jordan.hr: For the temporary letter: we can generate a proof-of-coverage PDF that states active enrollment dates, plan name (Redwood Core PPO), and insurer contact. It should not guarantee payment but helps scheduling. I can draft and attach.

sam.peopleops: Thanks. Member is traveling next week so timing is urgent. Any suggested text for the clinic to include when resubmitting?

alex.benefits: Ask them to: 1) include the prior auth number PA-8821 in field 23; 2) correct billing provider NPI/TIN to the entity on file (we can confirm which one insurer has); 3) include copy of signed referral if requested. Also request 'reconsideration' or 'reprocessing' code on the claim form.

lena.peopleops: I can pull the EOB and member's portal upload link and DM the member. @benefits-bot, can you generate the standard proof-of-coverage template for me to review? :pray:

benefits-bot: Generating proof-of-coverage template... Template ready: "Redwood Inference — Proof of Coverage (does not guarantee claim payment). Active member: [NAME], Plan: Redwood Core PPO, Coverage dates: 01/01/2026 - 12/31/2026. For claim inquiries call insurer at 1-800-555-0199."

jordan.hr: That looks good. Add a line: "If you need prior authorization details for scheduling, provide PA-8821 to the clinic billing team."

sam.peopleops: Perfect. Lena — can you also include the recommended claim remark text for the clinic? Something like: `Please reprocess claim with corrected billing provider NPI/TIN and apply prior authorization PA-8821; original denial due to provider credential mismatch.`

lena.peopleops: Yep. I'll DM the member the proof PDF + a short script for the clinic and the portal upload instructions. I'll also open an escalation ticket with insurer once clinic confirms resubmission.

alex.benefits: If insurer pushes back, escalate to medical appeals with EMR showing PT plan tied to post-op care. Keep receipts and itemized sessions.

sam.peopleops: Thank you all — I'll follow up with the employee and post updates here. :thumbsup:
